title: Deploy gate (warn-only) when tier is burning error budget + override logging
creator: Aisha Bello
body:
Context
- As part of tiered SLOs + error budget enforcement, we need to prevent “shipping into a fire” when a tier is actively burning budget.
- This ticket covers Phase 1: warn-only deploy gate. It must not block deploys yet, but must be loud, consistent, and auditable.

Goal
- Add a CI/CD (and optionally manual deploy) gate that evaluates the current error budget state for a given tier (Hosted vs Dedicated) and emits a warning when:
  - budget burn is above a configured burn-rate threshold OR
  - remaining budget is below a configured threshold.
- Gate is WARN-ONLY in this phase: deployments proceed, but warnings are surfaced in:
  - CI output
  - Slack notifications
  - a central audit log (including override reason when provided)

Non-goals (Phase 1)
- Hard-blocking deploys. That is ENG-4941.
- Automating rollback.
- Per-customer gating for Dedicated accounts. This phase is tier-level (Hosted / Dedicated) only.

Requirements
1) Budget state lookup
- The gate consumes budget state from the error budget computation job output (ENG-4934).
- Source of truth: a small HTTP endpoint or config-backed artifact published per tier/region that includes:
  - remaining_budget_fraction (0.0–1.0)
  - burn_rate_short_window (e.g., 5m/30m)
  - burn_rate_long_window (e.g., 1h/6h)
  - timestamp of last successful computation
  - data_quality status (OK / STALE / MISSING)
- If data_quality is STALE/MISSING, the gate should WARN with “budget unknown” (do not block in this phase).

2) Deploy context and tier mapping
- Gate must know what it is deploying and which tier(s) it impacts.
- Initial mapping proposal:
  - Changes in shared control-plane / gateway / routing / runtime services => impacts Hosted + Dedicated.
  - Changes scoped to dedicated-only deployment artifacts (e.g., dedicated routing policy pack, dedicated serving fleet images) => impacts Dedicated.
- Provide an explicit override flag to specify impacted tiers for edge cases (e.g., hotfix scoped to Dedicated EU only).

3) Warning behavior
- If tier is in a “red” budget state (exhausted or burning fast):
  - CI prints a structured warning block with links to:
    - Tiered SLO dashboard (Hosted/Dedicated)
    - Active burn-rate alert(s)
    - Mitigation runbook
  - Slack posts to #eng-sre and the service release channel.
- Thresholds should match the policy doc (multi-window burn-rate alerting approach):
  - Example (subject to final policy numbers): short-window burn > 14x AND long-window burn > 2x => “BURNING FAST”.
  - remaining budget < 25% => “LOW BUDGET”.

4) Override logging (auditable)
- Since this phase is warn-only, “override” means: the deployer acknowledges the warning and optionally provides a reason string.
- Gate records an audit event containing:
  - deploy id / build id
  - service / repo / commit SHA
  - impacted tier(s)
  - budget state snapshot (remaining + burn rates + timestamp)
  - actor (GitHub/CI user)
  - acknowledgement flag and free-text reason
- Audit log destination: existing deploy events stream (Telemetry) with a new event type, e.g., deploy_gate_budget_warning_ack.

5) UX / developer ergonomics
- Output must be readable in CI logs and copy/pastable into incident threads.
- Add a short “What to do next” section:
  - verify we’re not in an active incident
  - consider delaying non-critical changes
  - coordinate with IC if one is assigned
  - if shipping a mitigation, include “mitigation” in reason

Acceptance Criteria
- A deploy against any service that maps to Hosted or Dedicated triggers the gate check.
- When Hosted or Dedicated budget is “red” by threshold, gate emits warnings and posts to Slack.
- Warning includes links to dashboards/runbooks and the computed timestamp.
- Audit log event is emitted for every warning, including acknowledgement + reason when provided.
- If budget state is missing/stale, emits “budget unknown” warning and logs it.
- No deploy is blocked in this phase.

Implementation Notes
- Keep the policy thresholds in config (owned by SRE) rather than hard-coded in pipeline scripts.
- Ensure we do not introduce extra flakiness in CI: budget lookups should be time-bounded with fallback to “unknown”.
- Avoid calling Prometheus directly from CI; use the computed budget artifact/API.

Links / References
- Error budget computation pipeline: ENG-4934
- Burn-rate alerting: ENG-4930
- SLO config schema: ENG-4926
- Related next step (enforcement): ENG-4941

Risks / Open Questions
- Mapping deploys to impacted tier(s) for shared services may cause warning fatigue when only Dedicated is burning. Mitigation: allow explicit scoping flag + include data quality + tier statuses so warnings are actionable.
- Budget computation freshness: if the budget job is delayed, we may warn “unknown” too often. Track rate of unknown warnings as a health metric for the pipeline.

Rollout Plan
- Week 1: implement gate + warnings in one repo/service (control plane) behind a feature flag.
- Week 2: expand to gateway, routing, serving runtime repos.
- Week 3: enable Slack notifications by default.
- Collect feedback from on-call + release owners; adjust wording/links before enforcement phase.
comments: 2026-01-23 (Aisha Bello): Please keep this warn-only. We need signal before we start blocking deploys; also ensure we log every warning for later review of “risky deploys during burn”.

2026-01-27 (Connor O'Brien): Re: deploy-to-tier mapping—start conservative (assume shared services impact both tiers). Add an escape hatch flag so release captains can scope if necessary. We can refine mapping after 2–3 weeks of data.

2026-02-01 (Logan Wright): For audit logging, use the deploy events stream (Telemetry) and add a new event name. Please include commit SHA + CI actor + computed timestamp so we can correlate with burn graphs and incident timelines.
2026-02-05 (Jordan Lee): Implemented gate script with 2s timeout + fallback to BUDGET_UNKNOWN. Added structured CI block with links to tier dashboards and runbook. Working on Slack integration next.

2026-02-07 (Sahana Iyer): CI ergonomics: please ensure the warning block is single-line copyable JSON as well (for bots) + a human-readable section. Also, don’t make this a required check yet; keep it informational.

2026-02-12 (Jordan Lee): Landed in main behind flag. Enabled by default for control-plane and routing repos. Slack posts to #eng-sre on warning. Audit events showing up in telemetry-dev; will flip to prod after 24h.

2026-02-14 (Aisha Bello): Verified warning triggers correctly during synthetic “burning” state. Marking Done; follow-ups captured in ENG-4941 for enforcement and in ENG-4934 for freshness SLO on the budget artifact.
